name: Vegetarian Chalupas Poblanas

ingredients.name: vegetarian fresh white cheese made with vegetarian coagulants

steps: Combine masa harina and 3 g of the salt. Gradually work in the warm water to make a soft dough that does not crack when pressed. Cover and rest for 15 minutes. Meanwhile cook and cool the potato if it is not already prepared; cut it into small dice. Check that the white cheese is made with vegetarian coagulants.

Divide the dough into twelve small balls. Press each between sheets of plastic into a thin oval about 10 × 6 cm. Gently pinch the long sides up just enough to make a shallow boat shape, leaving the centre flat. Keep the ovals covered with a damp cloth while shaping the remainder.

Heat a wide heavy pan over medium heat with a thin layer of the measured neutral oil. Shallow-fry the ovals in batches for about 1–2 minutes per side until set and lightly golden, replenishing the measured oil as needed. Keep the shells slightly pliable rather than frying them into brittle tostadas; drain briefly on a rack.

Warm the green and red salsas separately until hot and season the diced potato with the remaining 2 g salt. Spread one tablespoon of green salsa on six warm chalupas and one tablespoon of red salsa on the other six. Divide the cooked potato, finely diced white onion and crumbled vegetarian cheese evenly over the twelve.

Serve immediately, three small chalupas per person. Alternate the red and green versions on a platter so the thin oval masa boats and modest toppings are visible. This Puebla-style preparation is intentionally smaller and flatter than a thick, loaded, round sope.
tips: Use vegetable oil rather than lard and verify the cheese label. Both salsas must be thick so they sit on the small oval bases. The reviewed photo shows six thin oval boats alternating red and green salsa with potato, white onion and cheese.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
